comparison: After assessments are sealed, an evaluator isolated from the assessor may compare each recommendation with the separately preserved outcome evidence.
dimensions: whether cited evidence supports the rationale at the cutoff
whether material cutoff-known uncertainty is preserved
whether the recommendation would have prioritized useful evidence at proportionate cost
whether a named cheaper or stronger cutoff-known alternative is supported
whether the falsification condition is observable and bounded
rules: No determination is scored as intrinsically favorable.
Later outcome agreement alone does not establish rationale quality.
Outcome facts must not be supplied to the assessor.
The evaluator records unsupported, hindsight-dependent, and indeterminate cases without repair.
Assessments remain non-authoritative and non-executable regardless of score.
